gen-dafont-sewer-sys-poppins: Horseshoe-shaped c's bent nearly shut give Sewer Sys its underground bite. It does the gritty, outlined shouting, while Poppins, a sans-serif with open curves and sturdy tall lowercase, does the patient talking.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-cascadia-c: Striking and a bit classic, SF Wonder Comic packs its words dense and tall through the middle. Cascadia Code, sans-serif and wire-thin, spaces its letters far apart and runs the same stroke around every bend, so it carries the quiet detail.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-cascadia-m: SF Wonder Comic leaves its bowls unfinished on one side, with stems just a shade heavier than the arms joining them. Cascadia Mono sits tight and ruler-straight beneath, so give it a little more size.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-julius-san: SF Wonder Comic has a mellow thick-thin shift and bowls left open on one side. Julius Sans One follows in a single nib's line with wide gaps between letters, so a long page would feel spacious and light.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-lexend-exa: SF Wonder Comic has a g with lightly thinned links and sturdy bowls, and the words look dense and tall in the middle. Lexend Exa is a plain sans with signage-like weight, wide curves and a big x-height.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-lexend-meg: SF Wonder Comic bends soft contrast into every curve and leaves its bowls unfinished. Lexend Mega, a plain sans drawn with one nib, keeps lowercase nearly capital height and a visible gap in each c, so a long text would read steadily and openly.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-lexend-pet: Lexend Peta reads wide-mouthed and sturdy, a sans-serif with big x-height, curves that never thin and a y whose tail matches its arm. And SF Wonder Comic, with its medium-range stroke modulation and tall dense words, adds the striking spark beside it.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-lexend-ter: SF Wonder Comic gives its bowls a gentle weight change where they curve, and leaves them unfinished on one side. Lexend Tera, a sans bent from a single length of wire, spaces its open-faced letters like stepping stones, which makes the page feel like a bold sign above a quiet path.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-lexend-zet: Lexend Zetta reads wide and tall-bodied, a sans with ribbon-like strokes of constant width. And SF Wonder Comic brings a brush-pressed softness above it, so give Zetta a little extra size to match its widely tracked stride.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-montserrat: Dense, tall-middled words with a subdued, striking contrast define SF Wonder Comic, and bowls stay unfinished on one side. Montserrat Alternates, a sans with constant-width arms and chalkboard lowercase, would read smoothly through a long page.
